thesis: The speaker argues that investors should adopt a private-equity mindset to look five to seven years ahead, aiming to own high-quality companies with growing competitive advantages and owner-oriented management teams on the right side of disruption. He emphasizes that over this long time scale, returns are driven by business outcomes rather than valuation changes, and he specifically advocates for buying growth stocks with 20 to 30 percent free cash flow yields to enterprise value while assuming multiple compression.
